name: c23_tools_intaglio_v2
prompt: Three identical square ancient Chinese bronze plaques side by side in one horizontal row with wide gaps between them, each exactly the same material, rim and rivets as the reference plaque (dark aged bronze, dull dark-teal verdigris patina, low raised rim border, four round rivets in the corners), seen perfectly straight on, flat frontal orthographic view. Each plaque has ONE pictorial image cut INTO the metal as INTAGLIO (sunken engraving): the lines are narrow V-shaped grooves chiselled below the flat surface, the groove bottoms filled with deep black shadow and grime, the groove edges catching a thin worn bright-bronze highlight on their lower-right side; the image is NOT raised, NOT embossed, NOT relief — it is incised lines only, like a Han dynasty stone line-engraving. NO text, NO letters, NO characters. LEFT plaque: a traditional Chinese drafting compass (gui): round hinge knob at the top, two long straight tapering legs spread apart in an inverted V, with a long incised circular arc swept between the two leg tips. MIDDLE plaque: a carpenter's try-square (ju): a large L-shaped ruler, upright, long arm vertical on the left and short arm horizontal at the bottom, both arms with fine incised tick marks. RIGHT plaque: an ancient balance scale: a vertical post, a level horizontal beam, two shallow round pans hanging on three thin lines each, perfectly level. Each engraving fills about 65% of its plaque and is clearly readable from far away. Even, dim, low-key light from upper left, slightly underexposed, desaturated. Background: flat solid pure black #000000, nothing else, no shadows on the background.
